results.content:
Jørgen Sandhaug

@internetyngve We use opengeni to build opengeni :D Btw suuper easy to deploy to any cloud or machine, e.g. your own vm behind tailscale or whatever, recommend trying that!

Atle Myhrer Knudtzon

Love that you are launching this to a wider audience!   
  
@We Are Learning have used @Opengeni for the last year, and I keep referring to @Opengeni for startups and scaleups that needs to be secure (SOC2 or similar) while using minimum bandwidth thinking about it.

Davlet Dzhakishev

@atlemk Appreciate support Atle! It's been amazing to work alongside great companies like @We Are Learning and make meaningful impact for growing scaleup needs.

Abdellatif Abdelfattah [...] Yngve

Congrats on the launch!!!  
  
Gotta deploy OpenGeni so i can use OpenGeni to deploy OpenGeni.  
  
I'm exited to see what you guys do in the space. This looks a lot more mature than the alternatives I've evaluated so far. It's the kind of thing that separates your product from "chatgpt api wrapper" to "yes, we run agents and we can tell you exactly how".

Davlet Dzhakishev

@internetyngve Haha, we were literally talking about this last week! In theory you can run Opengeni inside Opengeni inside Opengeni... all the way down, until the RAM gives up. 😅

Thanks a lot, that last line really made our day. Being able to show exactly what an agent did and can we trust them with important stuff is big reason we built this.

Jørgen Sandhaug [...] Hey Product Hunt! I'm Davlet from the Opengeni team.

For the past two years we've been running AI agents against real production cloud infrastructure at Cloudgeni. The model was never the hard part. Everything around it was: runs that die when a worker restarts, code that needs somewhere safe to execute, OAuth tokens for every user, tools to wire up, a human sign-off before anything risky, and a clear record of what the agent did and what it cost.

We kept rebuilding that layer, so we turned it into Opengeni.
